src: Eastmoney: CSI 300 index (000300), China 10Y government bond yield (CN10Y), Shanghai + Shenzhen margin financing balance (融资余额), 30Y CGB ETF 511090 and CSI 300 ETF 510300 turnover. Daily build in `daily` (every Shanghai session); the top-level series are weekly, last trading day of each week.

method.window: 4-week changes; z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks (min 26); thresholds ±0.5
components: Bond ETF turnover share: 4-week avg minus 26-week avg

method.window: 20-day changes; z-scores vs trailing 260 sessions (min 130); bond ETF share 20-day avg minus 130-day avg; thresholds ±0.5; hit rates over the next 20 sessions; margin balance as last published (one session behind)
components: Bond ETF turnover share: 20-day avg minus 130-day avg

notes.headline: Stocks bleed, bonds hold: margin sheds RMB81bn in 5 days as the CSI 300 hits a 17-month low; signal firms to +0.84 "bond rally"
notes.now: Leveraged money keeps leaving: margin financing fell another RMB15.6bn on Thursday to RMB2.193tn, down RMB81bn over five sessions, RMB234bn (9.7%) over 20 sessions and RMB818bn (27%) below the June 25 peak. The CSI 300 lost 0.76% to 3,955, a 17-month low and about 22% below its 52-week high, as a Wall Street AI sell-off (the Anthropic IPO fading, Korea and Japan down about 5%) hit chips and compute; ChiNext fell 3.5%, more than 5,200 stocks dropped and turnover rose to about RMB1.43tn. The national team again set the floor: the SSE 50 ETF and a CSI 300 ETF each traded a record RMB23–24bn, most of it in the last half hour, lifting banks to record highs and the SSE 50 into the green, after Thursday's RMB48bn of broad-ETF inflows; that equity-ETF volume is why the bond-ETF turnover share dropped to 26.4%. Bonds barely flinched: the 10Y on this panel edged up 0.4bp to 1.599%, 0.6bp above the Nov 6 record low of 1.593% (52-week high 1.916%; the CCDC curve in the recap above closed at 1.580%), and 511090 was flat at 121.61, as November's LPR was held for an 18th month and the PBOC drained RMB688bn net while overnight funding stayed at the 1.25% anchor. The Bond Rotation Signal rose to +0.84 (+0.71 yesterday, +0.75 five sessions ago, +1.27 twenty sessions ago) on day 52 of a rally episode that began Sep 2 and is worth 9.9bp so far. Margin outflow (−9.7% over 20 days, z −1.73) still does most of the work, with today's equity drop reviving the stock leg (CSI 300 −3.7% over 20 days, z −0.69) alongside the 10Y's 20-day fall (−5.0bp, z −0.74); bond-ETF share is neutral (z +0.20). The 130-day stock–bond correlation is only −0.07, so this is retail leverage draining into cash and duration while state money buys large caps, not a clean seesaw. Our read: keep a bond-rally bias for the next 2–4 weeks with the 10Y in a 1.55–1.63% range, grinding through the 1.59% low rather than gapping, since desks see little value in chasing toward 1.55% and the tax worry has cooled but not vanished; rally calls have been right about 72% of the time on the daily back-test (81% weekly), and a deeper equity rout without fresh easing would help bonds only slowly.
notes.flip: What would flip it: the 20-day window rolls onto a lower base over the next five sessions (CSI 300 3,986 and margin RMB2.357tn by Nov 27), so at flat levels the stock leg falls to about −0.8% and the margin leg to about −7.0%, pulling the signal toward the +0.5 threshold with no change in behaviour. A CSI 300 close back above about 4,100, margin rising above RMB2.30tn and the 10Y above 1.65% would take it to neutral or lower. The policy triggers are a formal move to tax new government-bond interest or a large equity-support package that revives leverage (bond-bearish), while an LPR or RRR cut would re-arm the bond rally.
phases: Equities slide, money hides in bonds

The CSI 300 fell 21% to 3,159 (Sep 13, 2024), close to multi-year lows. Margin debt shrank by about RMB160bn, and the 10Y rallied from 2.75% to 2.06%. Turnover in the 30Y CGB ETF rose roughly twentyfold. This is the textbook "asset scarcity" bond bull, and the signal was in rally mode through most of it.
Policy shock: the first big switch to equities

The PBOC's package (rate and RRR cuts plus equity swap and relending facilities) lifted the CSI 300 by 25% in six sessions. Margin debt rose about RMB290bn in five weeks, and the 10Y backed up about 12bp. The signal flipped to sell-off within a week. Because the easing was monetary, the bond sell-off stayed short.
"Moderately loose" pulls money back to bonds

After the Politburo shifted its stance, the 10Y dropped about 42bp in five weeks to 1.62%. Equities and leverage stalled, and the signal posted its best run, an 8-week rally call that was worth about −21bp.

Margin debt climbed RMB630bn (from RMB1.78tn to RMB2.41tn) as the CSI 300 rallied 21%. Funds sold duration: the 10Y rose 25bp to 1.90%, and 511090 fell about 6%. The stock–bond correlation was at its most positive here, so bond prices fell whenever stocks rose. The signal stayed in sell-off mode for 14 weeks and was right.

After margin debt peaked near RMB3.0tn in June, a RMB165bn one-week unwind (Jul 17) began the rotation back out of stocks. Margin debt is now down about RMB818bn (27%), and the CSI 300 is about 22% off its high (a 17-month low on Nov 20); it ended a record 12-week losing run in the week to Nov 6, helped by more than RMB600bn of stock-ETF inflows since late September, new stock-support steps (the SFISF swap, a 1% buyback-relending rate), a reported IPO pause and Central Huijin's new role as a quasi-stabilisation fund. Leverage has not returned, while PBOC bond buying, its redemption backstop (Oct 26) and the 1.25% overnight anchor support bonds; the 10Y hit a record-low 1.593% on Nov 6. The bond-interest tax story (Nov 11) and a fund-redemption wave then broke the seesaw for two weeks, with money parking in cash; by Nov 18–19 redemptions were fading, funds were buying long CGBs again and the 10Y returned to within 0.2bp of its low, while A-share turnover fell to a 2026 low and national-team ETF buying kept setting the equity floor, with record tail-end volume in the SSE 50 and CSI 300 ETFs on Nov 20 even as leverage kept draining.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows. Margin balance captures leveraged retail and hot-money equity flows. Bond ETF turnover share shows where trading activity is going, not net subscriptions. The back-test covers one rate cycle (Dec 2023 – Nov 2026), mostly a secular bond bull, so the 'rally' side has much more evidence behind it than the 'sell-off' side (44% hit rate, close to a coin flip). Treat a sell-off reading as a cue to cut duration, not to short. Hit rates use overlapping 4-week windows, which flatters them. Not investment advice.
